chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Mutayl narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Amr ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Aban ibn Taghlub. He said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, four thousand angels descended wanting to fight alongside al-Husayn ibn Ali (blessings of God be upon him), but they were not permitted to fight. So they went back to seek permission, and they descended [again], but al-Husayn (peace be upon him) had already been killed. So they are at his grave, disheveled and dusty, weeping for him until the Day of Resurrection, and their chief is an angel called Mansur (the Victorious).

key_terms.الاستئذان: Seeking permission - the angels sought divine permission to fight
key_terms.القتال: Fighting, combat - referring to the Battle of Karbala
key_terms.شعث غبر: Disheveled and dusty - description of perpetual mourning
key_terms.ملك: Angel (malak) - celestial being sent by God
key_terms.منصور: Mansur - meaning 'the victorious one', name of the chief angel
key_terms.يوم القيامة: Day of Resurrection - the final day of judgment

ai.seo_question: What is the hadith about four thousand angels at the grave of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates the account of four thousand angels who descended from heaven intending to support Imam al-Husayn (AS) at the Battle of Karbala (61 AH), but divine decree withheld their permission to fight. By the time they returned with permission, al-Husayn had already been martyred. These angels now remain at his blessed grave in a state of grief and mourning until the Day of Resurrection. This narration was shared in the scholarly assembly (majlis) of Sheikh al-Saduq in 368 AH, during the sacred month of Sha'ban, reflecting the community's devotion to commemorating the tragedy of Karbala.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. Matil narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi’l Khattab narrated to us from Musa b. Sa`dan from `Abdullah b. al-Qasim from `Amr b. Aban al-Kalbi from Aban b. Taghlub. He said: Abu `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as) said:

Four thousand angels came down to fight alongside al-Husayn b. `Ali (as), but they were not permitted to fight. So, they went back to seek permission, and they came down [again], but al-Husayn (as) had been killed. So, they are at his grave, disheveled and weeping, until the Day of Resurrection. Their chief is an angel called Mansur (the victorious one).
